expectations.text: Output contains 'Problem Statement' section
expectations.evidence: No 'Problem Statement' heading. Baseline opens with '## Overview' (line 3); there is no dedicated business/user problem section.

expectations.text: Output contains 'Scope' section
expectations.evidence: Line 16: '## Scope' heading present (rendered as an In Scope / Out of Scope table).

expectations.text: Output contains 'Capabilities' section
expectations.evidence: Line 27: '## Functional Capabilities' heading present. Section name differs slightly but is a capabilities section.

expectations.text: Output contains 'Dependency Map' section
expectations.evidence: No 'Dependency Map' section or capability-dependency table. The closest is a '## Processing Flow' ASCII diagram (line 134), which is not a dependency map keyed by capability IDs.

expectations.text: Output contains 'Open Questions' section
expectations.evidence: No 'Open Questions' heading anywhere in the output.

expectations.text: Output contains 'Research Suggestions' section
expectations.evidence: No 'Research Suggestions' heading. The output has an '## Optional Enhancements (Future)' section (line 235) but it lists feature ideas, not research topics to delegate.

expectations.text: Output contains 'Next Steps' section
expectations.evidence: No 'Next Steps' heading. The document ends at 'Optional Enhancements (Future)'.

expectations.text: Depth level is marked as 'quick'
expectations.evidence: No depth marker anywhere. There is no 'Depth: quick' line or metadata header.

expectations.text: Covers 1-3 capabilities (quick depth)
expectations.evidence: Functional Capabilities lists 8 numbered items (1. File Selection ... 8. Status & Notifications, lines 29-131), far exceeding the 1-3 quick-depth band.

expectations.text: Each capability has a Trigger field
expectations.evidence: Capabilities are bullet-described prose; none has a labeled 'Trigger' field.

expectations.text: Each capability has an Inputs field
expectations.evidence: No 'Inputs' field on any capability; capabilities are free-form bullet lists.

expectations.text: Each capability has a Logic flow field
expectations.evidence: No per-capability 'Logic flow' field. A single global 'Processing Flow' diagram exists (line 134) but capabilities lack individual logic-flow fields.

expectations.text: Each capability has an Outputs field
expectations.evidence: No 'Outputs' field on any capability.

expectations.text: Each capability has an Edge cases field
expectations.evidence: No per-capability 'Edge cases' field. Error scenarios are collected in a single 'Error & Rejection Cases' table (line 205), not attached per capability.

expectations.text: Each capability has a Connects to field
expectations.evidence: No 'Connects to' field on any capability; there are no capability IDs to connect.

expectations.text: Business problem is stated in Problem Statement
expectations.evidence: No Problem Statement section; the Overview (lines 5-12) describes what the feature does, not the business problem it solves.

expectations.text: User problem is stated in Problem Statement
expectations.evidence: No Problem Statement section and no explicit user-problem statement; Overview is feature-description prose.

expectations.text: Success criteria are measurable
expectations.evidence: No 'Success criteria' field. An 'Acceptance Criteria' checklist exists (lines 219-231) which is measurable, but it is not the success-criteria element within a Problem Statement that the assertion targets, and there is no success-criteria field present.

expectations.text: Logic flows describe WHAT not HOW (no tech stack, no code, no architecture)
expectations.evidence: Output is heavily implementation-oriented: 'magic-byte type detection' (line 148), 'emitted in an efficient format (e.g., WebP)' (line 106), 'EXIF and other embedded metadata ... removed' (line 108), 'durable object store' (line 116), 'Direct-to-storage (presigned) uploads' (line 242), 'chunked upload' (line 40). These are HOW/architecture/tech details.

expectations.text: Dependency Map uses CAP-01 format for capability IDs
expectations.evidence: No CAP-NN identifiers anywhere; capabilities are numbered 1-8 and there is no Dependency Map.

expectations.text: Research Suggestions reference the researcher skill
expectations.evidence: No mention of the researcher skill or any research delegation in the document.

expectations.text: Does NOT attempt to save/persist the output — suggests librarian skill instead
expectations.evidence: No librarian skill suggestion. The document neither persists itself nor recommends the librarian skill; it simply ends with Optional Enhancements. The librarian-handoff behavior is absent.

expectations.text: Does NOT attempt to conduct its own research — flags topics for researcher skill
expectations.evidence: No researcher-skill delegation and no flagged research topics; the output asserts best practices directly (e.g., re-scan on signature update, presigned uploads) without flagging them for research.

expectations.text: Checks for existing knowledge via librarian skill before starting
expectations.evidence: No Existing Knowledge section and no librarian lookup; the document starts directly with an Overview.

expectations.text: Flags at least one topic as needing research (e.g., virus scanning approaches, thumbnail generation)
expectations.evidence: No topic is flagged as needing research; virus scanning and thumbnailing are described as settled design with prescriptive choices.

expectations.text: Document is written to ./solution-architect/{slug}.md
expectations.evidence: Output is at outputs/file-upload.md; not written to a ./solution-architect/{slug}.md path, and the document contains no reference to that convention.

expectations.text: Output ends with a suggestion to use librarian skill for persistence
expectations.evidence: Document ends at '## Optional Enhancements (Future)' (line 235); no librarian persistence suggestion.

expectations.text: Edge cases cover missing/invalid input scenarios
expectations.evidence: The 'Error & Rejection Cases' table covers invalid input: 'File > 10 MB → Rejected', 'Disallowed type → Rejected', 'Extension ≠ real content → Rejected', 'Corrupt / unparseable → Rejected' (lines 209-212). Not attached per capability, but missing/invalid input scenarios are covered.

expectations.text: Edge cases cover dependency failure scenarios
expectations.evidence: Dependency failures are covered: 'Scan unavailable → Pending' (line 214), and the Virus Scanning section: 'Scan error / timeout → file remains pending; the upload is retried or flagged for manual review' (lines 89-90).

expectations.text: Connects to references other capability IDs or explicit '—' for standalone capabilities
expectations.evidence: There are no capability IDs and no 'Connects to' fields; inter-capability relationships are only implied via the Processing Flow diagram, not via ID references.

claims.claim: Output is a well-structured, security-conscious file-upload feature description
claims.evidence: The baseline is thorough and technically sound (quarantine-first scanning, magic-byte detection, metadata stripping). It is good engineering prose but does not follow the solution-architect prescribed format.

claims.claim: Capabilities are decomposed with per-capability structured fields
claims.evidence: Capabilities are free-form bullet lists with no Trigger/Inputs/Logic flow/Outputs/Edge cases/Connects-to fields.

claims.claim: Output delegates research and persistence to companion skills
claims.evidence: No reference to researcher or librarian skills; the baseline operates fully self-contained.

needs_review: Baseline run used no skill, so absence of the prescribed structure (CAP-NN, Problem Statement, Dependency Map, Open Questions, Research Suggestions, Next Steps, librarian/researcher delegation) is expected.

suggestions.assertion: Edge cases cover missing/invalid input scenarios
suggestions.reason: This and the dependency-failure-coverage assertion are content-level and not format-specific, so they pass even for the no-skill baseline. They are weakly discriminating between with-skill and baseline since any competent feature write-up covers these. Consider tying them to the per-capability 'Edge cases' field to test the prescribed structure rather than mere presence.

Not satisfiable under the eval harness output redirection (deliverables land in outputs/), so it fails for both runs regardless of behavior. Revise to check the slug filename or the in-document declared path.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions discriminate strongly between skill and baseline (baseline 4/29 vs with_skill 27/29). Most structural assertions correctly fail for the baseline. The two content-only edge-case assertions are the least discriminating, and the ./solution-architect/{slug}.md path assertion is unsatisfiable under the harness.
